about: Evidence behind the resume: the facts strip on Home, a receipt for every headline number, and (once written) the decisions, incidents and screen-call answers rendered on Proof Hub. Every receipt field is written from the resume's own wording (resume-ats.txt, proof-hub.html); fields nobody has documented yet are null and the panel says so. Entries marked "draft": true and keys starting with "_" are author notes: scripts/strip_drafts.py removes them at deploy, so they never reach the live site (they are visible in this public repository). scripts/check_evidence.py lints this file in CI.

provisioning-time.headline: ≈10 min → <1 min per device
provisioning-time.claim: Cut device provisioning from roughly 10 minutes of manual work to under 1 minute per device.
provisioning-time.baseline: Roughly 10 minutes of manual, console-driven onboarding per device: registration, certificate generation and bootstrapping.
provisioning-time.result: Under 1 minute per device with a repeatable workflow aligned to AWS IoT Core and enterprise security practices.
provisioning-time.role: Delivered the greenfield CLI and supporting APIs; integrated AWS Secrets Manager and Auth0 credential handling.
provisioning-time.confidence_note: The figures are approximate ("roughly 10 minutes" to "under 1 minute") and how they were timed is not documented here yet.
provisioning-time._todo: Who timed it, when, and how (one device, wall clock?). Then set confidence to "measured" and method to that sentence. Attach a redacted terminal timing or CI log as the artifact ({"label": "...", "href": "..."}).

payload-bytes.headline: 476 B → 15 B
payload-bytes.claim: MQTT delta updates cut constrained-device payloads by about 40%, with one example dropping from 476 bytes to 15 bytes.
payload-bytes.baseline: The same device update before delta messaging: 476 bytes.
payload-bytes.result: 15 bytes for that update after switching to MQTT delta updates; across messages the reduction was about 40%.
payload-bytes.method: Byte count of one message before and after the change.
payload-bytes.confidence_note: 476 → 15 is one example, not the average. The average reduction was about 40%.
payload-bytes._todo: Fill the "payload" block below with a sanitized before/after pair (field names changed, structure and sizes real); check_evidence.py then verifies the byte counts and Home animates the real squeeze.

portal-volume.claim: A client-facing payment portal processed roughly 250,000 payments totalling about $85M.
portal-volume.baseline: What the number is: payments processed through the portal while in production.
portal-volume.result: Zero reported payment failures attributable to the platform; still in production after handoff.

etl-hours.headline: 1,200+ hours · ~$40K
etl-hours.claim: An automated data-entry program (Java + MS SQL Server) saved more than 1,200 hours of manual work and about $40K.
etl-hours.baseline: A manual data-entry process that consumed a large amount of repetitive effort and introduced error risk.
etl-hours.result: The program handled parsing, validation, transformation and persistence without human intervention, with no ongoing support burden.
etl-hours.confidence_note: More than 1,200 hours and about $40K, as stated on the resume; how they were counted is not documented here yet.
etl-hours._todo: State how the 1,200 hours were counted (minutes per record × records, over what period) and the hourly rate behind $40K; then set confidence to "measured", "logged" or "estimated" and method to that sentence.
